current_repo_note: The licence was plain MIT when added on 2026-01-21 and was changed on 2026-02-21 to MIT with a rider that grants no rights to OpenAI, Anthropic, their affiliates, or anyone acting for them.
canonical_data: assignments with claim, reservation and dispatch state, runtime work and coordination counters, send operations and routing state in a local SQLite database, plus a versioned JSON assignment store and a command-policy file in the project
strengths: Assignments are persisted before each external step with claim, file-reservation and dispatch states, and the code recovers lost or stranded dispatches, which is orchestration state a terminal manager does not keep
Safety is a policy layer: a project policy file blocks or requires approval for destructive command patterns, with an approval engine behind it
A coordinator scores which agent should take which unit of work, weighing critical path, file overlap and token budgets, and exposes the same surface to scripts through robot-mode JSON commands
weaknesses: The licence is MIT with a rider that names OpenAI and Anthropic as restricted parties, bars anyone acting for them, defines use to include executing and testing, and ends all permissions on breach; it is not an open-source licence
Agent state is read from tmux screen text with per-agent patterns, and the README calls the tool intentionally tmux-centric
Inter-agent mail and the task graph depend on separate tools the author also publishes, and the README says advanced workflows degrade when they are absent
A 59.8 MB compiled Linux binary is committed to the repository, the cost table is dated May 2025, and the repository has a single maintainer
why_it_matters: Shows how far a tmux-centred tool can go before it becomes orchestration: persisted assignments, policy, and a scoring coordinator, under a licence that singles out two model vendors.
